skill.name: scaffold-exercises
skill.description: Create course exercise directories with sections, variants, readme stubs, lint checks, and Git-friendly moves.
skill.summary: Scaffold lint-ready course exercise folders and readme stubs.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown inline-code or fence false positives, not Ruby backtick execution. The skill does contain intended guidance to run pnpm, git, and mkdir commands, so those external-command findings are confirmed as medium-risk workflow behavior. No prompt injection, network access, credential access, or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: External commands can change the user workspace.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user confirmation before running git commit, git mv, or other commands that modify tracked files.

remediation.issue: Scaffold paths may be derived from a user plan.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize names to lowercase dash-case and restrict generated paths to the exercises directory before using mkdir or git mv.

remediation.issue: The pnpm lint command executes local project tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Run pnpm ai-hero-cli internal lint only inside the intended course repository and report failures before making further changes.

content.value_statement: Course authors need consistent exercise folders that pass repository lint rules. This skill turns a section plan into structured exercise directories, readme stubs, and validation steps.
actual_capabilities: Creates numbered section and exercise folder plans from a course outline.
Defaults new exercise stubs to explainer folders unless variants are specified.
Creates readme stub requirements for problem, solution, and explainer variants.
Uses repository lint rules to check exercise structure and missing files.
Guides Git-friendly exercise renames with git mv.
Documents expected readme and main.ts requirements for exercise variants.
limitations: Designed for repositories that use the ai-hero-cli exercise lint rules.
Does not generate full lesson content beyond basic readme stubs.
Requires user review before shell or Git commands modify the workspace.
Does not verify course pedagogy or exercise difficulty by itself.

use_cases.title: Create a New Course Section
use_cases.description: Turn a planned section into numbered exercise folders with explainer, problem, and solution variants.

use_cases.title: Standardize Exercise Stubs
use_cases.description: Create readme files and folder structures that satisfy repository lint expectations before content writing begins.

use_cases.title: Renumber Existing Exercises
use_cases.description: Move exercises with Git-aware commands while preserving history and keeping numeric prefixes ordered.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold One Exercise
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single stub.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an explainer-only exercise for section 01 named Retrieval Basics. Use the repository naming rules and include a minimal readme stub.

prompt_templates.title: Create Section From Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Build several exercises from a short outline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scaffold section 03, Query Design. Add three exercises: Introduction, Filters with problem and solution, and Evaluation. Run the lint check after creating the stubs.

prompt_templates.title: Add Variant Folders
prompt_templates.scenario: Expand an existing exercise with learning variants.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update exercise 02.04 so it has explainer, problem, and solution folders. Add non-empty readme stubs and explain any lint issues you find.

prompt_templates.title: Renumber a Section Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Renumber section 05 so the memory exercises appear after the retrieval exercises. Use git mv for path changes, then run the exercise linter and summarize the final structure.

output_examples.input: A request to create section 05 with three memory exercises.
output_examples.output: A created section folder with three numbered exercise folders, each containing the requested variant folders and readme stubs.

output_examples.input: A request to add problem and solution variants to an existing explainer exercise.
output_examples.output: The exercise now includes problem and solution folders with readme stubs, followed by a lint result summary.

output_examples.input: A request to rename an exercise while preserving history.
output_examples.output: A Git-aware move plan, updated folder names, and a final check that the numbering remains ordered.

best_practices: Provide the target section number, exercise names, and requested variants before scaffolding.
Review planned shell and Git commands before allowing workspace changes.
Run the repository lint command after each batch of scaffold changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use free-form folder names that ignore the numeric prefix rules.
Do not commit generated scaffolds before reviewing the created files.
Do not add empty placeholder files that the lint rules explicitly reject.

faq.question: What repositories is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for course repositories that use exercises folders and ai-hero-cli lint rules.

faq.question: Can it create complete exercise content?
faq.answer: It mainly creates structure and basic readme stubs. Full lesson writing still needs author input.

faq.question: Does it run shell commands?
faq.answer: It may suggest or run mkdir, pnpm lint, and Git commands when the user approves workspace changes.

faq.question: How are exercise folders named?
faq.answer: Sections use a two digit prefix, and exercises use section and exercise numbers with dash-case names.

faq.question: Can it rename existing exercises?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends git mv so repository history is preserved during renames.

faq.question: What should I provide in my prompt?
faq.answer: Provide the section number, section title, exercise titles, and which variants each exercise needs.
